title: Grade 9 Biology National Exam & Practice 2015 (6 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 6 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: One of the following renowned Ethiopian biologists has developed a vaccine for the rinderpest disease.
questions.explanation: Professor Tilahun Yilma developed the vaccine for rinderpest, a viral disease that affects cattle and other cloven-hoofed animals.

questions.questionText: A grade nine student has planned to study animal cells using a compound light microscope. She prepared a slide of stained human cheek cells for this purpose. Which one of the following activities should she first do?
options: Set up the microscope with the lowest power objective in place.
Adjust the iris diaphragm until the maximum brightness is coming.
Looking through the eyepiece lens to move the objectives down.
Using coarse focusing knob to rotate the nosepiece for a higher magnification lens.
questions.explanation: When using a microscope, the correct first step is to start with the lowest power objective lens to easily locate the specimen before increasing magnification.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about plant cells? They have
options: Vacuole which controls all activities of the cell.
Cell wall which gives support and strength to the cell.
Chloroplast which is filled with sap, liquids and minerals.
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose that provides structural support and strength.

questions.questionText: A plant cell is placed in a solution which has lower solute concentration than its contents. After a few minutes the cell will become
questions.explanation: When a plant cell is placed in a hypotonic solution (lower solute concentration outside), water enters the cell by osmosis, making it turgid.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about human food digestion?
options: Mouth use protease enzyme to breakdown proteins.
The stomach physically breaks down the ingested food.
The small intestine is site of absorption of digested molecules.
Large intestine is the site of lipid hydrolysis.
questions.explanation: The small intestine is responsible for the absorption of nutrients after digestion, including amino acids, sugars, and fatty acids.

questions.questionText: Which of the following enzymes is correctly matched to the food stuff it acts on?
questions.explanation:
Pepsin is a digestive enzyme found in the stomach that breaks down proteins into smaller peptides.
 Maltase acts on maltose (a sugar), trypsin acts on proteins, and amylase acts on starch, not fats.

questions.questionText: Which of the following breathing movements happens when air enters into and exits from the balloon lungs in the bell-jar model?
options: Air enters when the rubber sheet is pushed up.
Air enters when the bell-jar thorax contracts.
Air exits when the balloon lungs have higher pressure than the external environment.
Air exits when Y-piece is rotated both clockwise and counterclockwise.
questions.explanation: In the bell-jar lung model, air enters the balloons (lungs) when the rubber sheet (diaphragm) is pulled down, creating low pressure inside. Air exits when the lungs have higher pressure than the external environment, causing exhalation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following structures of the heart is correctly matched with its function?
options: Left ventricle - contracts and forces oxygenated blood around the body
Right atrium - contracts and forces deoxygenated blood into the lungs
Left atrium - contracts and forces blood into the right ventricles
Right ventricle - contracts and forces blood into the left ventricles
questions.explanation:
The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the aorta to the rest of the body.
 The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs, not to the left ventricle.

questions.questionText: Suppose your friend fails suddenly due to heart attack while he is playing football. The victim needs artificial breathing to keep him alive until medical support arrives. Which activity is strictly prohibited in this situation?
options: Open the airway by removing any obstacles from the mouth
Remove any obstacle from the mouth that might block the airway
Give mouth-to-mouth resuscitation if he is conscious
Make sure the airway is open and the head is tilted back
questions.explanation:
Mouth-to-mouth resuscitation should only be performed if the person is unconscious and not breathing.

 If the person is conscious, it is dangerous and unnecessary, so it is strictly prohibited.

questions.questionText: In the diagram showing blood circulation system in the human body, the parts indicated by numbers 1, 2, 3, and 4 are respectively:
options: Pulmonary artery, pulmonary vein, vena cava, aorta
Aorta, vena cava, pulmonary vein, pulmonary artery
Vena cava, pulmonary artery, aorta, pulmonary vein
Pulmonary vein, aorta, vena cava, pulmonary artery
questions.explanation: Blood leaves the left ventricle through the aorta to the body, returns via the vena cava, goes to the lungs through the pulmonary artery, and returns oxygenated via the pulmonary vein. Therefore, the correct order is: aorta → vena cava → pulmonary vein → pulmonary artery.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences is correct about the activities of the heart?
options: Diastole is when the heart muscles contract and force the blood out.
Systole is when the heart muscles relax and it fills with blood.
The noise of heartbeat one hears through a stethoscope is the sound of valves.
As the heart beats blood travels through the arteries with a uniform pressure.
questions.explanation: The 'lub-dub' sound of the heartbeat heard through a stethoscope is produced by the closing of heart valves — the 'lub' is due to atrioventricular valves closing, and the 'dub' due to semilunar valves closing.

questions.questionText: During culturing micro-organisms, all of the following activities are important EXCEPT:
options: transferring target micro-organisms into an agar medium.
tilting the lid of the  Petri dish during inoculation.
adding distilled water to a sterilized agar.
questions.explanation:
Sterilizing inoculating loops, transferring microorganisms into agar, and slightly tilting the Petri dish lid during inoculation are important aseptic techniques.

 However, adding distilled water to already sterilized agar is unnecessary and may introduce contamination.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following diseases can be caused by more than one type of microorganism?
questions.explanation:
Gastroenteritis (inflammation of the stomach and intestines) is a general syndrome that can be caused by various pathogens, including different bacteria (like Salmonella or E. coli), viruses (like Rotavirus), or parasites.

 The other options are typically caused by a specific microorganism (Typhoid by Salmonella typhi, Tuberculosis by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and Cholera by Vibrio cholerae).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following diseases is correctly explained with its causes or symptoms?
options: Gonorrhoea is caused by Treponema pallidum.
Syphilis has sore ulceration on the genitals as a symptom.
Syphilis is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
Gonorrhoea has a burning sensation symptom while urinating.
questions.explanation:
Gonorrhoea is a common sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and a key symptom is often a painful or burning sensation while urinating (dysuria).

 Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum, and while it causes a sore (chancre), the first option incorrectly matches the cause of Gonorrhoea with Syphilis.

questions.questionText: The names of which two taxa are used in binomial nomenclature?
options: The highest and the lowest unit of classification
The two highest units of classification
The two lowest units of classification
The two middle units of classification
questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature, the two-part naming system for organisms, uses the Genus and the Species names, which are the two most specific and therefore the two lowest units of the standard taxonomic hierarchy (Kingdom -> Phylum -> Class -> Order -> Family -> **Genus** -> Species).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following phyla is characterized by a flexible cartilaginous rod-like structure, that runs along the dorsal side of the body?
questions.explanation: The flexible cartilaginous rod-like structure described is the notochord, which is a defining feature of the phylum Chordata.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following groups of organisms is correctly matched with its phylum?
questions.explanation:
Starfish belong to the phylum Echinodermata (spiny-skinned animals).

 Snail belongs to Mollusca, Earthworm to Annelida, and Fish to Chordata.

questions.questionText:
A zoologist studied 5 vertebrate species (spA, spB, spC, spD and spE) and described their features as follows: 

spA: Smooth moist skin; pass parts of their lives in water and on land. 

spB: streamlined body with scales; gills for gaseous exchange.

 spC: feathers over the body with scales on legs; endothermic; horny beak.

 spD: Dry skin covered by scales; lungs for respiration.

 spE: mammary glands; endothermic; high internal body temperature.

 Based on the features listed above, spA, spB, spC, spD and spE can be classified under the vertebrate classes respectively:
options: Pisces, Amphibia, Aves, Reptilia, and Mammalia.
Amphibia, Pisces, Aves, Reptilia, and Mammalia.
Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia, and Pisces.
Pisces, Aves, Reptilia, Mammalia, and Amphibia.
questions.explanation:
Based on the features:

- spA: smooth, moist skin; lives in water and on land → Amphibia

- spB: streamlined body, scales, gills → Pisces (fish)

- spC: feathers, beak, endothermic → Aves (birds)

- spD: dry scaly skin, lungs → Reptilia (reptiles)

- spE: mammary glands, endothermic → Mammalia (mammals)

questions.questionText: Which one of the following events happens during carbon cycle? Carbon dioxide is:
options: removed from the air by animals during respiration.
returned into the air by plants during photosynthesis.
transferred from plants to animals by their feeding relationship.
absorbed from air when microbes decompose plant and animals.
questions.explanation:
In the carbon cycle, carbon is fixed into organic molecules by plants (photosynthesis).

 This organic carbon is then transferred from plants to animals when the animals consume them (feeding relationship).

questions.questionText: Which of the following plant adaptation mechanisms helps cactus to adapt in the desert environment?
options: Spreading its seeds in wider areas.
Increasing number of stomata in its leaves.
questions.explanation: Cacti are succulents; their primary adaptation to the arid desert is the ability to store large amounts of water in their fleshy stem tissues.

questions.questionText: Consider the following diagram demonstrating the pyramid of energy. Which of the following is INCORRECT about the above pyramid of energy?
options: The organisms of the first trophic level convert light energy into chemical energy.
The organisms of each trophic level use large proportion of the energy to build their body.
The amount of energy transferred through the trophic levels drops with each step up of the pyramid.
The energy lost as heat to the surrounding in each trophic level is insignificant.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which kingdom contains organisms that lack cell walls but have complex, specialized tissues (like nervous and muscle tissue)?
questions.explanation: Animals lack cell walls and possess unique nervous and muscle tissues.

questions.questionText: The two reverse processes that play a significant role in absorbing and releasing carbon dioxide, respectively are
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to produce glucose, while respiration releases carbon dioxide as glucose is broken down to produce energy.

questions.questionText: An organism having the following characteristics can be grouped under animals.
options: Prokaryotic cell, cell wall and respiration
Autotroph, movement and response to stimuli
questions.explanation: Animals are eukaryotic, multicellular, heterotrophic organisms (many of which breathe/respire). They lack cell walls, prokaryotic structures, or autotrophic capabilities.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the binomial nomenclature?
options: The genus name is written in English while the species name is written in Latin.
The first letter of genus name is capitalized while the species name is written in small letters.
Both genus and species names are capitalized and italicized when printed.
The genus name is written in full while the species name is abbreviated.
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the genus name's first letter is capitalized, and the species name is written in small letters (and both are typically italicized or underlined).

questions.questionText: The primary component of the cell membrane that is responsible for its flexibility is:
questions.explanation: The fluidity of the lipid bilayer allows the cell membrane to change shape.

questions.questionText: The term Pathogen refers to any organism that:
options: Lives in a stable, mutualistic relationship with a host.
questions.explanation: Pathogen means 'disease-causing agent,' including bacteria, viruses, fungi, and protozoa.

questions.questionText: Which part of the female reproductive system receives the fertilized egg and is the primary site of implantation?
questions.explanation: The uterus is where the embryo implants and the fetus develops.

questions.questionText: The institute of biodiversity conservation is one of the biological research institutes of Ethiopia attempting to conserve the genetic resources of the country. As such, the institute's major research efforts focus on all of the following EXCEPT
questions.explanation:
A biodiversity conservation institute focuses on the preservation of living organisms (plants, animals, microorganisms).

Soil conservation** is a broader environmental concern, not a primary focus of genetic conservation.

questions.questionText: The ability of a living organism to maintain relatively constant internal conditions is known as:
questions.explanation: Living things can maintain relatively constant internal conditions, a characteristic referred to as homeostasis.

questions.questionText: Which component of the cytoskeleton provides strength and acts as 'tension-bearing' elements?
questions.explanation: Intermediate filaments reinforce cell shape and fix organelle location.

questions.questionText: Why are arctic animals such as seals, walruses and whales large in body size? To
options: move in the water bodies easily
questions.explanation: According to Bergmann's rule, endotherms in colder climates tend to be larger because a large body size has a smaller surface-area-to-volume ratio, which helps reduce heat loss.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following adaptations is important for survival of polar bear in very cold environments? Having
questions.explanation:
Polar bears rely on insulation to survive in the Arctic.

 Their most crucial adaptation for cold environments is a thick layer of fat called blubber under the skin.

 This layer provides excellent thermal insulation and also acts as an energy reserve. They also have dense fur, but the blubber is the primary thermal barrier.

questions.questionText: Biology is defined as the scientific study of:
options: The physical world and its phenomena
The composition and structure of matter
questions.explanation: The term 'Biology' comes from the Greek words 'bios' (life) and 'logos' (study), meaning the scientific study of life or living things.

questions.questionText: In the context of the female reproductive system, what does the term Menarche refer to?
options: The cessation of the menstrual cycle (menopause).
The beginning of the menstrual cycle in puberty (first period).
questions.explanation: Menarche is the medical term for the first menstrual period.

questions.questionText: Biological magnification (or bioaccumulation) refers to the increasing concentration of toxic substances in organisms at progressively higher:
questions.explanation: Toxins accumulate because they are consumed faster than they are metabolized or excreted as you move up the food chain.

questions.questionText: The type of birth control pill that prevents ovulation by providing a continuous, high level of synthetic hormones is classified as a:
questions.explanation: Contraceptive pills use synthetic estrogen and progesterone to suppress the hormonal signals needed for ovulation.

questions.questionText: The Cervix is the narrow structure that connects which two parts of the female reproductive tract?
questions.explanation: The cervix is the lower, narrow part of the uterus that opens into the vagina.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following alternatives contains only protein rich cereals?
options: Red kidney peas, maize and white pea
White kidney peas, red kidney peas and chickpea
Wheat, red kidney peas and sesame
questions.explanation: White kidney peas, red kidney peas, and chickpeas are legumes, which are rich in protein. Cereals like wheat, maize, and barley contain some protein but are not as protein-dense as legumes.

questions.questionText: In the scientific method, if a hypothesis is not supported by experimental data, the scientist should:
options: Discard the experiment and start over
Force the data to fit the hypothesis
Propose a new or alternate hypothesis
questions.explanation: If a hypothesis is not supported by experimental data, one can reject it and try to come up with alternate explanations (new hypotheses).

questions.questionText: The ecological process that takes place on abandoned agricultural land after a fire, where soil is already present, is called:
questions.explanation: Secondary succession occurs in an area where a previous community existed and soil is still intact.

questions.questionText: The condition resulting from a chronic deficiency of protein and energy in the diet, leading to stunted growth, thinness, and fatigue, is generally known as:
questions.explanation: Undernutrition, encompassing conditions like Kwashiorkor (protein deficiency) and Marasmus (energy/protein deficiency), is a major form of malnutrition.

questions.questionText: The specific role or job of an organism in its environment, including all biotic and abiotic factors it utilizes, is its:
questions.explanation: The ecological niche is the way an organism fits into its environment, including what it eats and how it lives.

questions.questionText: In which phase of the menstrual cycle does the uterine lining (endometrium) rebuild itself following menstruation, driven primarily by Estrogen?
questions.explanation: The proliferative phase is when Estrogen stimulates the regeneration of the endometrium.

questions.questionText: Which infectious agent is responsible for causing Genital Warts and is also linked to cervical cancer?
questions.explanation: HPV is the viral agent responsible for genital warts and is a major cause of cervical cancer.

questions.questionText: In which type of asexual reproduction does a new organism develop from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site, as seen in yeast and Hydra?
questions.explanation: Budding is the formation of a small outgrowth (bud) that eventually detaches to form a new, independent organism.

questions.questionText: A substance, often a weakened or killed form of a pathogen, administered to stimulate the immune system to produce memory cells without causing the disease is a(n):
questions.explanation: Vaccines provide active immunity by preparing the immune system to fight a future infection.

questions.questionText: The five kingdoms of life were developed in a classification scheme proposed by:
questions.explanation: The five-kingdom system of classification is the scheme developed by Robert Whittaker.

questions.questionText: The disease Cholera is caused by a bacterium and is spread primarily through:
questions.explanation: Cholera causes severe diarrhea and dehydration, typically from ingesting water or food contaminated with the Vibrio cholerae bacterium.

questions.questionText: This item is based on the following diagram of simple food chain. Leaves -> Grasshoppers -> Rodents -> Leopards. What will happen if the number of rodents significantly decrease? There will be
options: an increase in the number of leopards.
no change in the number of leopard.
an increase in the number of grasshoppers.
questions.explanation:
In the given food chain, rodents feed on grasshoppers. If the number of rodents decreases, there will be less predation on grasshoppers, leading to an increase in their population. 

The number of leopards may eventually decrease due to reduced food availability (rodents).

questions.questionText: In the human diet, which food group is the most important for growth and repair of body tissues?
questions.explanation: Proteins are the building blocks of cells, tissues, enzymes, and hormones.

questions.questionText: The tool primarily used by biologists for observing extremely small micro-organisms like viruses, which uses a beam of electrons, is the:
questions.explanation: Electron microscopes use a beam of electrons (instead of light) and electromagnets (instead of glass lenses) to achieve higher magnification, necessary for observing extremely small entities such as viruses.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a safety rule when dealing with chemicals in the laboratory?
options: Wear a disposable respirator mask when handling toxic chemicals
Never allow laboratory chemicals to contact your bare skin
Always put chemicals open after use
Do not pour unused (left over) chemicals back to its original container
questions.explanation: A key rule is to never put chemicals open and to not return unused chemicals to the original container.

questions.questionText: A biological community consists of the different species within an area and the interactions among these species. Which of the following is an example of such an interaction?
questions.explanation: Interactions within and among species in a biological community include predation, parasitism, herbivory, competition, and pollination.

questions.questionText: If you are asked to write the taxonomic hierarchy of modern human being from the kingdom downwards, what will be the correct sequence the taxon?
options: Animalia → Hominidae → Mammalia → Primata → Homo → Chordata → Homo sapiens
Animalia → Mammalia → Chordata → Hominidae → Primata → Homo → Homo sapiens
Animalia → Chordata → Mammalia → Primata → Hominidae → Homo → Homo sapiens
Animalia → Primata → Mammalia → Chordata → Hominidae → Homo → Homo sapiens
questions.explanation: The taxonomic hierarchy of humans from Kingdom down is: Kingdom (Animalia) → Phylum (Chordata) → Class (Mammalia) → Order (Primata) → Family (Hominidae) → Genus (Homo) → Species (Homo sapiens).

questions.questionText: The structural difference between the Rough ER and Smooth ER is the presence or absence of:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are attached to the Rough ER, making it appear 'rough'.

questions.questionText: A balanced diet must include adequate amounts of:
options: All six major nutrient groups in correct proportions.
questions.explanation: A balanced diet ensures adequate intake of carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals, and water.

questions.questionText: The Fluid Mosaic Model suggests that the cell membrane is:
options: dynamic structure where proteins float in a fluid lipid bilayer.
Identical in structure to the cell wall.
questions.explanation: The model emphasizes the fluid movement of lipids and proteins.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is well justified, why the left ventricle is tough in nature? because it
options: forces oxygenated blood out of the heart.
returns deoxygenated blood to the heart.
returns oxygenated blood to the heart.
forces deoxygenated blood out of the heart.
questions.explanation: The left ventricle has thick, muscular walls because it must generate high pressure to force oxygenated blood through the aorta and the entire systemic circulation.

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes the importance of studying biology?
options: It only helps in understanding complex mathematical formulas.
It helps understand how living things work and interact with the environment, and is applied in medicine and agriculture.
It is solely concerned with the history of the natural world.
It is only useful for identifying rock formations.
questions.explanation: Studying biology helps to understand how living things work, how they function and interact with the environment, and is critical for advancements in medicine and agriculture.

questions.questionText: A compound light microscope with two eye-pieces is referred to as:
questions.explanation: A compound light microscope with a single eye-piece is called monocular; one with two eye-pieces is said to be binocular.

questions.questionText: Assume you wanted to demonstrate compatibility of blood groups. You took four test tubes labeled O, A, B, and AB based on the blood group that each test tube contains. Then you added unknown blood sample into each test tube and no agglutination was observed in each test tube. From this, you can conclude that the unknown blood sample was
questions.explanation:
If no agglutination occurred in test tubes containing blood groups O, A, B, and AB, it means the unknown sample had no A or B antigens.

 Blood group O has neither A nor B antigens on its red blood cells, so it does not react (agglutinate) with anti-A or anti-B antibodies.

 Therefore, the unknown blood sample is blood group O.

questions.questionText: In an experiment, students wanted to prove that enzymatic digestion begins in the mouth using certain chewed food coated with their own saliva. In order to get a positive result for their experiment, what type of food sample and testing solution should the students use?
questions.explanation:
Saliva contains the enzyme amylase, which breaks down starch into maltose.
 To demonstrate enzymatic digestion in the mouth, students can use bread (rich in starch) coated with saliva.

 Copper sulphate solution (Benedict's test) can then detect the presence of reducing sugars, indicating that starch has been digested into maltose.

questions.questionText: Organisms in Kingdom Protista are all:
questions.explanation: Protists are the most diverse kingdom, but the one thing they all have in common is that they are all eukaryotes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about Prokaryotic cells is correct?
options: They are generally larger than eukaryotic cells.
They have a simple, single, circular DNA molecule.
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic DNA is typically circular and singular.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about the conservation mechanism of wild life?
options: Indigenous practices relay on the use of taboos for conservation of plants.
Modern practices relay on growing invasive plants in mountainous area in order to prevent soil erosion.
Controlled wildlife hunting areas can't be considered one of the conservation mechanisms.
Wild life conservation is selective protection of a species with economic significances and eliminating less valued species.
questions.explanation: Indigenous conservation strategies traditionally rely on social norms, sacred groves, and cultural taboos to restrict the exploitation of specific plant and animal species.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an organism that primarily reproduces asexually through fragmentation?
questions.explanation: Starfish (sea stars) are famous for regenerating entire bodies from a severed arm, a form of fragmentation.

questions.questionText: The primary advantage of asexual reproduction for an organism in a stable, unchanging environment is that it:
options: Requires two parents, ensuring gene mixing.
Is rapid and energy-efficient for mass production of identical offspring.
Creates offspring with better survival rates against diseases.
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction is fast and cost-effective, producing many genetically identical offspring quickly, which is ideal if the current environment is favorable.

questions.questionText: Suppose you took a container and divided it into two halves by a membrane which is permeable to water and labelled the two halves " A " and " B ". Finally you added hypertonic solution in " A " and hypotonic solution in " B ". What will be the expected result of this experiment? The water level of
options: both " A " and " B " rise up.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: If a plant reproduces asexually through a rhizome (underground stem), the offspring are genetically:
options: More resistant to disease than the parent.
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction, including vegetative propagation via rhizomes, produces clones that are genetically identical to the parent.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest and basic unit of living things?
questions.explanation:
A cell is the smallest and the basic unit of living things.
All living things are composed of cells.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an organism composed entirely of prokaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria are prokaryotes (Monera).

questions.questionText: What is the name for the uncondensed, dispersed genetic material (DNA and proteins) found in a non-dividing eukaryotic cell?
questions.explanation: Chromatin is the relaxed form of DNA during interphase.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered part of the Endomembrane System?
questions.explanation: The Endomembrane System includes the nuclear envelope, ER, Golgi, lysosomes, vacuoles, and plasma membrane.

questions.questionText: Organisms that are capable of withstanding a narrow range of environmental conditions are called:
questions.explanation: Steno- means 'narrow,' indicating a narrow tolerance for factors like temperature or salinity.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a feature of Octopi and squid in phylum mollusca? They have
options: segmented body with head and thorax.
hard muscular foot with a hard body.
questions.explanation:
Octopi and squid are Cephalopods, the most highly evolved class of Molluscs.
 They are known for having the most complex nervous system among invertebrates, including a large, doughnut-shaped, well-developed brain enclosed in a cartilaginous cranium.

 They breathe using gills (not lungs), have a soft, unsegmented body, and their muscular foot is modified into arms/tentacles.

questions.questionText: Which Ethiopian plant is an endemic species often found in the Afroalpine zone and plays a role in local medicine and cultural practices?
questions.explanation: Hagenia abyssinica is a prominent endemic Afromontane tree with medicinal uses.

questions.questionText: Compared to the inhaled air what are the percentage of nitrogen, oxygen and carbon dioxide gases in exhaled air, respectively?
questions.explanation:
Inhaled air contains approximately 78–79% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 0.04% carbon dioxide. 

Exhaled air has roughly the same nitrogen content (≈80%), reduced oxygen (≈16%) due to cellular respiration, and increased carbon dioxide (≈4%) from metabolic processes.

questions.questionText: The process of adding a micronutrient, such as Iodine to salt or Vitamin A to flour, to a common food item to prevent deficiency is called:
questions.explanation: Food fortification is a public health strategy to address widespread micronutrient deficiencies.

questions.questionText: Assume your friend has a blood type that has no antigen on his red blood cells but produces antibodies a and b, loses blood due to a car accident. If blood transfusion is necessary to save his life, your friend can receive blood from someone with
questions.explanation:
The friend's blood has no antigens on the red blood cells but produces antibodies a and b.

 According to the ABO blood group system, this description corresponds to blood type O. Individuals with blood type O are universal donors but can only receive blood from other type O individuals, as receiving A, B, or AB blood would trigger a severe reaction from their anti-A and anti-B antibodies. 

Therefore, the friend can receive blood from someone with blood type O.

questions.questionText: What is the most accurate measure for determining a child's nutritional status regarding stunting (chronic undernutrition)?
questions.explanation: Height-for-age is the indicator used to diagnose stunting, which is the result of long-term inadequate nutrition.

questions.questionText: Organisms belonging to Kingdom Monera are primarily characterized as:
options: Heterotrophic and possess cell walls made of chitin
questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera consists of simple **prokaryotic** and **unicellular** organisms that lack a well-defined nucleus or any membrane-bound organelles.

questions.questionText: Which kingdom contains heterotrophic organisms that typically obtain nutrients by absorption and have cell walls, often made of chitin?
questions.explanation: Kingdom Fungi are heterotrophs that obtain nutrients from nonliving organic matter, and they are not photosynthetic.

questions.questionText:
Three students carried out different experiments in exhaled air as indicted below. 

Student I - uses cold glass and blue cobalt chloride paper.

 Student II - uses ice cubes. 

Student III - uses tube containing lime solution and straw. 

Based on their setup, which students will get positive results to demonstrate the presence of water vapor and carbon dioxide, respectively?
questions.explanation:
Student I's setup with a cold glass and blue cobalt chloride paper can demonstrate water vapor: the water vapor from exhaled air condenses on the cold surface, and cobalt chloride paper changes color when it absorbs moisture.

 Student III's setup with lime solution (calcium hydroxide) and a straw can demonstrate carbon dioxide: CO₂ from exhaled air reacts with limewater to form a milky precipitate of calcium carbonate.

 Student II's use of ice cubes alone will not provide a positive test for either water vapor or CO₂.

questions.questionText: The highest level of organization in ecology, which encompasses all life on Earth and the parts of the Earth where life exists, is the:
questions.explanation: The biosphere is the global ecological system integrating all living beings and their relationships.

questions.questionText: Vast areas of grassland with scattered trees, experiencing a wet season and a prolonged dry season, are typical of the:
questions.explanation: Savannas are tropical and subtropical grasslands, often found in parts of Africa, including Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: From the following alternatives select the common features that are found both in animal and plant cells.
options: Cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, lysosome and Golgi apparatus
Cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum
Cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, chloroplast and Golgi apparatus
Cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, large vacuole and Golgi apparatus
questions.explanation:
Both plant and animal cells share common organelles such as the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and endoplasmic reticulum.

 Chloroplasts and large central vacuoles are typically found only in plant cells, while lysosomes are more prominent in animal cells.

questions.questionText: The process of releasing a mature ovum from the ovary into the fallopian tube, typically occurring around day 14 of the menstrual cycle, is called:
questions.explanation: Ovulation is the release of the egg from the ovary, triggered by a peak in Luteinizing Hormone (LH).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following nutrients is correctly matched with its primary role to the human body?
questions.explanation: Lipids (fats) serve as long-term energy storage and thermal insulation to maintain body heat reserve.

questions.questionText: Which of the following organisms is an example of a unicellular organism?
questions.explanation:
Unicellular organisms consist of a single cell.
Paramecium is given as an example of a unicellular organism.

questions.questionText: What is the primary consequence of thinning the ozone layer in the Earth's stratosphere?
options: Increased ultraviolet (UV) radiation reaching the surface
questions.explanation: The ozone layer absorbs harmful UV radiation; its depletion leads to higher UV exposure.

questions.questionText: Which term describes a group of individuals of the same species living in the same area at the same time?
questions.explanation: A population is defined as a collection of individuals of a single species in a given geographical area.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the feature of kingdom Monera? Its members are
questions.explanation:
Kingdom Monera (now largely obsolete, replaced by Archaea and Bacteria) consists of Prokaryotes.
 Prokaryotic organisms are typically unicellular and lack a membrane-bound nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. They are described as being without separated nucleus (meaning the genetic material, the nucleoid, is not enclosed by a membrane).

questions.questionText: Which characteristic is unique to organisms in the Kingdom Animalia when compared to plants and fungi?
options: They lack structural support of **cell walls**.
questions.explanation: Unlike plants and fungi, animals lack the structural support of cell walls.

questions.questionText: Which disease is caused by a protozoan parasite and transmitted by the tsetse fly?
questions.explanation: African Sleeping Sickness is caused by Trypanosoma parasites carried by the tsetse fly.

questions.questionText: Which statement about eukaryotic cells is false?
options: They include plant, animal, fungal, and protist cells.
They have linear DNA organized in a nucleus.
questions.explanation: All cells (prokaryotic and eukaryotic) contain ribosomes.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following Ethiopian biological research institutes is known for housing a major gene bank in Africa?
questions.explanation: The Institute of Biodiversity Conservation (IBC) in Ethiopia is renowned for maintaining one of the largest gene banks in Africa, preserving seeds and genetic materials of various plants for conservation and research purposes.

questions.questionText: The process of amniocentesis is often used during pregnancy to:
options: Determine the sex of the fetus.
Obtain amniotic fluid for genetic testing of the fetus.
questions.explanation: Amniocentesis is a medical procedure used to collect fluid for the prenatal diagnosis of chromosomal abnormalities and genetic disorders.

questions.questionText: Which human activity most significantly disrupts the natural water cycle by increasing runoff and reducing infiltration and groundwater recharge?
questions.explanation: Paving roads and building structures prevents water from soaking into the ground (infiltration), increasing surface runoff.

questions.questionText: What is the primary danger of contracting **Typhoid Fever**, a bacterial disease spread by contaminated food/water?
options: Severe intestinal damage and systemic infection
questions.explanation: Typhoid fever causes prolonged fever, abdominal pain, and can lead to internal bleeding or perforation of the intestine.
